purpose: Settle whether always-applicable authoring guidance can be reached by skill discovery at all. The skill's own subject is a moment users rarely verbalize -- nobody says 'I am naming an export' -- so its description was aimed at the diagnostic and review moments instead. These cases test whether that aim was enough, and whether the authoring path needs a routing line from the always-loaded global rules.

run_contract.installed_collection: Discovery is a contest, not a test in isolation. Every case MUST run with the full deployed skill collection installed, because a negative result may mean another skill won rather than that this one failed. Record which skill loaded instead, never just that this one did not.

known_competitors.python-code-style: Deployed third-party skill whose description covers naming conventions and triggers on writing new code. It is a broader-triggering competitor for exactly the authoring moment authoring-no-cue probes, and its naming advice is PEP 8 style rather than findability. A Python authoring case is included to measure this directly.
known_competitors.writing-for-humans: Owns prose; near-miss-prose measures whether it wins.
known_competitors.global WORKFLOW.md: Its Structure section carries the abstract version of this skill's naming rule and is always loaded, so it may satisfy the model without any skill loading at all.

clients.reason: Only Claude Code exposes a reliable skill-load trace. The skill deploys to OpenCode, Copilot CLI and Codex as well, but activation there cannot be observed with the same confidence, so a result from those clients would not be comparable.
clients.if_extended: Record the client per run and do not pool results across clients.

conditions.setup: The user-level workflow instructions carry no pointer to this skill. This is the shipped state as of 2026-09-03.

The Structure section of the user-level workflow instructions carries a clause naming this skill for the authoring moment. Add it for the duration of the run and remove it afterwards unless the result argues for keeping it.
conditions.scope: Run condition B for authoring-no-cue and python-authoring only. The other cases do not depend on it, and running them twice buys nothing.

decision_rule.authoring-no-cue: The case that decides the skill's shape, and the reason this file exists. Compare condition A against condition B. A fails and B passes: the routing line earns its always-loaded cost, so keep it and keep the skill. Both fail: discovery cannot reach this content by any available means, and it belongs in a rules file rather than a skill -- this is a real possible outcome, not a formality. Both pass: the routing line is unnecessary and should not be added.
decision_rule.reading_predictions: Each case carries should_trigger, the desired outcome, separately from predicted_A, what I expect to observe under condition A. Where they disagree the case is an open question, not a defect -- do not score a matching prediction as a pass or a matching desire as a success.
decision_rule.near_miss_threshold: A near-miss case triggering in 3 of 5 runs means the description is over-broad. At 1 or 2 of 5, treat it as noise rather than signal; this sample cannot distinguish a weak tendency from chance.
decision_rule.sample_size_caveat: Five runs per case per condition is enough to separate never from usually. It cannot measure a small difference, so do not report a percentage.

cases.prompt: I keep grepping for where we send the webhook and finding nothing useful. Help me sort this out.
cases.reason: A failed search is the loudest symptom of the problem this skill prevents, and the skill now carries the recovery steps that serve it. A first review found this case dishonest: the description advertised the diagnostic moment while the body held only authoring rules, so loading it here answered a question it could not address. The 'When a search comes up empty' section was added in response.
cases.also_observe: Whether the agent applies the recovery steps rather than only restating naming rules. Activation without recovery behavior means the section is present but not doing the work.

cases.prompt: This function does something different from what it used to. What should it be called now?
cases.reason: Renaming on a behavior change is a rule the skill states directly.

cases.prompt: Review the naming in this pull request.
cases.reason: Reviewing names is the skill's subject stated in the user's own words.

cases.prompt: Add a function that validates the SMTP config.
cases.reason: The authoring moment, with no naming or search vocabulary in the request. Desired and predicted deliberately disagree under condition A: this is the open question the eval exists to settle, not a defect to be scored as failure.
cases.also_observe: Whether the resulting function is named as this skill would advise even when the skill did not load. The always-loaded workflow rules already say to use clear names, so a good name here is not evidence that discovery worked.

cases.prompt: Write a helper in this Python module that reads the retry settings.
cases.reason: The same authoring moment in a language where a deployed competitor exists. python-code-style triggers on writing new code and covers naming conventions, so it may win the slot with PEP 8 advice that says nothing about findability. Prediction under B is left open because the routing line is language-neutral and its effect against a language-specific competitor is genuinely unknown.
cases.also_observe: Which skill loaded instead, if any. A loss to python-code-style is a different finding from no skill loading at all: the first is a routing contest this skill can lose on wording, the second is the reachability problem.

cases.prompt: We build our analytics event names by interpolating the entity and the action. Is that a problem?
cases.reason: Directly the whole-literals rule, phrased as a question rather than a naming task.

cases.prompt: Reformat this file to match the project style.
cases.reason: Formatting is not findability, and a formatter already owns it.

cases.prompt: Split this 400-line module into smaller functions.
cases.reason: Module structure, governed by the global workflow rules rather than this skill.

cases.prompt: Improve the wording in this README.
cases.reason: Prose belongs to writing-for-humans; this skill covers code identifiers and literals.

cases.prompt: Should this state be a discriminated union or a struct with nullable fields?
cases.reason: Type design was deliberately excluded from the skill; triggering here would mean the description overclaims.

cases.prompt: This codebase is really hard to work with. Where would you start?
cases.reason: Findability is one plausible reading among several, so either loading the skill or asking what makes it hard is defensible.
